purpose: Adds a default-off loadAllCoreBlockAssets setting that registers the WP 6.9+ should_load_separate_core_block_assets opt-out filter (registered pre-init at priority 10) so classic themes can restore the combined wp-block-library stylesheet, suppresses the legacy 6.8 on-demand filter only while the opt-out is active, adds a defensive combine_css guard that never folds wp-block-library into the minified bundle when separate core block assets are active, and ships a new PHPUnit/Brain-Monkey test suite.
riskRationale: Core filter-precedence logic is verified correct against WP 6.9 source (the priority-10 __return_false overrides core's priority-0 __return_true and makes wp_load_classic_theme_block_styles_on_demand() bail), the setting is additive/default-off, and lint/test/build gates pass. Risk is elevated by repo-process and test-infra defects rather than runtime logic: the full dev/test vendor tree (~35MB, ~4,735 files) was committed to tracked vendor/ against the AGENTS.md production-only convention (its composer autoload_files.php would load PHPUnit/Mockery/Brain-Monkey helpers on every request for git-based installs), the new PHP suite hard-depends on patchwork.json being at the process CWD and silently breaks outside the repo root, the combine_css guard has zero test coverage, and a stale combined-CSS cache path can keep serving the monolith to 6.8->6.9 upgraders until the cache is cleared.
breakingChanges: Dev-only test dependencies (PHPUnit, Brain Monkey, Patchwork, Mockery, PHPCS/WPCS stack, etc., ~35MB) are now tracked in the git vendor/ tree, changing repository layout, size, and dev-install behavior.
The new default-off 'Load Combined Core Block Styles' toggle changes front-end CSS loading on WP 6.9+ when explicitly enabled (the opt-out overrides the 6.8 on-demand toggle).

text: The WP 6.9 block-assets reconciliation is well-researched and functionally correct: the opt-out precedence, pre-init timing, 6.8 backward-compat gating, and combine_css guard all match WP core semantics, and the new 5-test suite genuinely runs under PHPUnit 11 (composer test previously reported green while executing zero tests because the legacy class-*-test.php files do not match the *Test.php discovery convention). The blocking problems are repo hygiene and test infrastructure: the commit tracks the entire dev/test vendor tree, the PHP suite hard-depends on patchwork.json being at the process CWD, the combine_css guard has no automated coverage, and stale combined-CSS caches can undermine the fix for 6.8-to-6.9 upgraders until the cache is cleared.

reasoning: Functionally sound, backward-compatible, and verified end-to-end (lint:js, composer lint, npm test, composer test, npm run build all pass), but the PR should not merge as-is: it commits ~35MB of dev/test dependencies into the tracked vendor/ tree against the documented production-only-vendor convention, and the new PHP test suite silently breaks outside the repo root because patchwork.json is read from the process CWD. Regenerate vendor with `composer release`, add the dev-only directories to .distignore, and make the test bootstrap CWD-independent before merge.

message: The opt-out precedence gate is correct: $is_69_optout_active requires both the setting and function_exists('wp_load_classic_theme_block_styles_on_demand'), and the filter is registered at plugin load (before init) at default priority 10, which runs after core's priority-0 __return_true and wins. A false return makes core's wp_load_classic_theme_block_styles_on_demand() bail before registering the on-demand filter and late-style hoisting, so the opt-out is a genuine full opt-out and the 6.8 filter is suppressed only while it is active.

The combine_css guard sits inside the per-handle loop before fetch/dequeue and shares the same source of truth as the filter logic: wp_should_load_separate_core_block_assets() is evaluated once per request, so wp-block-library is skipped only when separate assets are active, is still combined when the opt-out is active, and WP 6.8 behavior is untouched via the function_exists() gate. The monolith can never be re-forced into the head by the combiner.

The loadAllCoreBlockAssets default is additive (false) and every read uses ! empty(), so existing installs without the key degrade safely to false with no migration; sanitize_settings_recursively() already casts booleans, and the JS defaultSettings merge and the built bundle contain the new key.

The new suite constructs a real Main() and asserts actual filter-registration state via Brain Monkey Filters has() across the full 6.8/6.9/opt-out-wins/both-on precedence matrix (5 tests / 10 assertions pass under PHPUnit 11) — a genuine improvement over the pre-existing class-*-test.php files that PHPUnit 11 never discovers.

The commit tracks the entire dev/test dependency tree in git vendor/ (~4,735 files / ~525K lines: phpunit, brain/monkey, antecedent/patchwork, mockery, hamcrest, sebastian, nikic/php-parser, phar-io, theseer, myclabs, staabm). This contradicts AGENTS.md, which requires committing production-only vendor via `composer release` (base master tracked only the production packages). Beyond repo bloat and history pollution, the committed vendor/composer/autoload_files.php registers dev-only entry points, so a git-based install loading the plugin pulls PHPUnit/Mockery/Brain-Monkey helpers into memory on every request until `composer install --no-dev` is run. The release ZIP currently stays clean only because CI runs composer install --no-dev; .distignore does not list the new dev packages, so a skipped or stale packaging step would ship test frameworks to production.
suggestion: Regenerate vendor production-only before committing (composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader, then re-add vendor/), keeping dev tooling available via `composer dev-setup`, and add the new dev-only vendor directories (antecedent, brain, phpunit, mockery, hamcrest, sebastian, nikic, phar-io, theseer, myclabs, staabm) to .distignore as defense-in-depth.

message: The new PHP test suite hard-depends on patchwork.json being at the PHPUnit process CWD. Patchwork reads patchwork.json from getcwd() at init and the suite stubs function_exists via Patchwork's Functions when() helper; removing repo-root patchwork.json makes all 5 tests fail with the Patchwork Exceptions NotUserDefined error, and running phpunit from tests/php/ fails too. Any CI or IDE run from a subdirectory silently breaks the entire PHP suite (PHPUnit reports errors, not tests-not-found), and marking an internal function redefinable process-wide is heavy-handed for exercising one function_exists guard.
suggestion: Make the run deterministic on CWD: chdir() to the project root at the top of tests/php/bootstrap.php before any Patchwork initialization, or emit a clear error if patchwork.json is absent; consider refactoring the function_exists guard into a small seam so it can be tested without Patchwork redefining internals.

message: The new guard only affects freshly-built combined CSS; the cache-freshness loop (lines 282-304) iterates only the currently-queued sources and re-serves the cached index.css when nothing is newer. On a 6.8-to-6.9 upgrade with combineCSS enabled, the cached combined file was built while wp-block-library was in the queue (full monolith), and after the upgrade wp-block-library is no longer queued so no source is newer — the stale monolith keeps being served in the head (defer_stylesheets also skips wppo-combine-css) until the cache is manually cleared. A WP core version bump does not invalidate this cache, partially defeating the fix for upgraders. Relatedly, the freshness loop still includes wp-block-library in its mtime comparison even though the combine loop now skips it, forcing pointless re-minification in an edge case.
suggestion: Invalidate or version the combined-CSS cache when the effective separate-assets state changes: include wp_should_load_separate_core_block_assets() state (and the option value) in the combined-file cache key/version, or clear the combined-CSS cache on the upgrader_complete hook for WP core upgrades. Also apply the same wp-block-library skip inside the freshness loop for consistency.

message: The combine_css guard is the second half of this fix but has zero automated coverage: the new suite only asserts Main::setup_hooks() filter registration, and the legacy class-cache-test.php does not run under PHPUnit 11. The guard's behavior (wp-block-library skipped when separate assets are active, combined when the opt-out is active) is asserted nowhere, leaving the part most likely to regress untested.
suggestion: Add a PHPUnit test that drives Cache::combine_css() with a stubbed $wp_styles registered/queue and a stubbed wp_should_load_separate_core_block_assets(): assert wp-block-library is neither fetched nor dequeued when the function returns true, and is still combined when it returns false.

message: should_load_separate_core_block_assets -> __return_false is a global filter with no theme-type guard. On WP 6.9 the opt-out affects block themes as well as classic themes (reviewers diverge on the exact priority outcome — whether the plugin overrides the block-theme default or loses the collision — but both readings leave block-theme behavior unintended), silently undoing the block-theme separate-assets default even though the setting targets classic themes and shortcode compatibility. It is opt-in and default-off, so not a functional break, but block-theme users can inadvertently change payload behavior.
suggestion: Gate the opt-out to classic themes with ! wp_is_block_theme() (re-checking the filter priority against core's _add_default_theme_supports()), or at minimum document in the UI description that the toggle also affects block themes.

message: The five pre-existing test files (class-cache-test.php, class-rest-test.php, class-core-tweaks-test.php, class-database-cleanup-test.php, class-image-optimisation-test.php) do not match the PHPUnit 11 *Test.php suffix and remain silently skipped — only MainBlockAssetsTest is discovered, so composer test reports green with 5 tests while the legacy Cache/Rest/Core_Tweaks/DB/Image suites never execute. The PR documents that composer test previously ran zero tests but leaves the dead files in place, giving a false sense of coverage.
suggestion: Rename the legacy files (and classes) to the *Test.php convention and migrate Brain Monkey 1.x APIs (for example replace Anything() with the 2.x equivalent) so the full suite runs under PHPUnit 11, or delete the stale files and document that only MainBlockAssetsTest is runnable.

message: The function_exists stub returns false for every non-target function, driving unrelated branches in Main::__construct() to their fallback paths (for example wp_should_output_buffer_template_for_enhancement and wp_script_add_data), so the harness never exercises the real 6.9 runtime path (template-enhancement buffer plus late-style hoisting) together with the opt-out; a future constructor change depending on one of these returning true would regress silently.
suggestion: Delegate non-target function names to the real function_exists so only the target functions are faked, keeping the rest of the constructor on its true branch; optionally extend the stub so wp_should_output_buffer_template_for_enhancement returns true on the simulated 6.9 path.

message: The new Load Combined Core Block Styles toggle renders interactively on all WP versions even though it is inert below 6.9 (PHP gates on function_exists), so on WP 6.8 a user can enable and save it with no effect; when both toggles are on, the on-demand toggle is silently overridden with no UI indication.
suggestion: Gate the field's disabled state on the WP version (and ideally theme type) exposed via wppoSettings so the toggle only appears where it has effect, and surface a small notice when both blockAssetsOnDemand and loadAllCoreBlockAssets are enabled explaining that the combined-library setting takes precedence on 6.9+.

message: The new translatable strings (Load Combined Core Block Styles and the updated Load Block Assets On Demand description) are absent from the tracked languages/performance-optimisation.pot, whose POT-Creation-Date predates this change, so the strings remain untranslatable until the POT is regenerated.
suggestion: Run `composer makepot` after the build so the new and modified FileOptimization strings are extracted, and commit the regenerated POT.
